threads.thread_goal: Align on current workflow and define target process scope

messages.text:
Kicking off the work on the standardised accounting and inventory process for moving services (project_pack_ref: Standardised Accounting and Inventory Process for Moving Services).
To get started on T1, can everyone share how a move currently flows from first customer contact through to invoice and ledger posting?
From my side, I will start mapping the steps into A1 so we can see the end-to-end picture.
Key questions:
- Where do we consider the process to start: first quote, or only once a job is confirmed?
- At what point do we say the process ends: when the invoice is sent, or when it is posted and paid?
- Which data do movers already capture that we actually use in accounting?
Please reply with a short outline of the steps you follow today, and any pain points you see between movers and bookkeepers.

From the truck side, this is roughly what happens now:
- Ops calls or messages me with the address, date, and rough volume.
- I note it in my notebook and load the tools I think we need.
- On site, I write down start time, finish time, and any extra stops, but it is not on a standard sheet.
- If there is damage or extra work, I just write a short note or send a photo.
- At the end of the day, I send photos of my notes to the office or drop the paper on the desk.
Pain points:
- Sometimes I forget to write the customer name clearly, so the office calls me back.
- I do not always know which details matter for the invoice, so I may skip distance or waiting time.
Happy to adjust if we can make it simple enough to fill in between loading and unloading.

On the accounting side, for a typical move I see this flow today:
1) Ops emails or drops off a job note with customer name, date, and sometimes hours.
2) I create the sales invoice in the system based on that note.
3) I apply the standard moving service VAT code and post to the moving revenue account.
4) I attach the job note as support and post the invoice.
5) Later, when payment comes in, I match it to the open invoice.
Gaps:
- Job notes are inconsistent, so I often have to call the mover to confirm hours, extra services, or travel time.
- Sometimes I am missing the correct customer address or tax number, which delays issuing the invoice.
- We do not have a clear rule on when a job is considered complete for invoicing, especially if there are multiple days.
For A1 and T1, I can help document at least five recent moves with all these steps and highlight where we lose time or information.

Adding to what was shared:
- Sometimes the first contact is only a phone call and we do not keep a record until the job is confirmed.
- For some customers we send a quote first, but the quote is in a separate file and not linked to the final invoice.
- For multi-day moves, I have seen partial notes for each day, which makes it harder to see the full job cost and revenue.
I think for A1 we should include the quote step as well, even if we later decide the standard process officially starts at confirmation.
On the end point, I would lean towards ending the process when the invoice is posted in the ledger, and treat payment and reminders as part of a separate collection process.

I can help with T1 by pulling a few recent invoices and matching them to the job notes we received.
One thing I am not fully sure about is whether we should include the payment matching step in this same process map or keep it separate.
Also, for movers data, I often see only total hours and no breakdown of driving versus loading, and I do not know if we need that split for accounting or just for operations.
Maybe we can clarify what is really mandatory for the books versus nice to have for planning.

Thanks all, this is very helpful.
On start and end points, here is a proposal for us to react to:
- Start: when a move is confirmed with the customer (accepted quote or verbal confirmation) and we have at least customer name, address, date, and agreed service.
- End: when the invoice is posted in the ledger with the correct VAT and supporting job documentation attached.
Payment collection would then sit in a separate process.
On data from movers, from an accounting and tax perspective, I see the following as candidates for mandatory fields:
- Customer name and address
- Job date(s)
- Description of service (e.g. local move, long-distance, packing included)
- Hours worked and rate basis (hourly or fixed price)
- Any extra billable items (packing materials, extra stops)
- Confirmation that the job is completed
Let us discuss if this list is realistic on the truck side before we lock it in for A1 and the later job sheet in A2.

From the truck, your list mostly works, but I want to check a couple of points:
- For description of service, would a few standard options help, like local move, long-distance, packing, storage? That would be faster than writing long text.
- For hours, I can record start and end time and breaks. If you need the split between driving and loading, I can try, but it may slow us down.
- Extra billable items: I can tick boxes for packing materials and extra stops, and maybe write a short note if something unusual happens.
If we keep it to ticks and short numbers, I can fill it in between tasks without holding up the team.

On the accounting side, I do not need a detailed narrative for every job, but I do need enough to justify the invoice if we are audited.
Standard options for service type would be fine as long as they map clearly to the correct revenue account and VAT code in A3 later.
For hours, total billable hours per job are essential. The split between driving and loading is more for operations, so I would not make that mandatory for accounting.
I would add one more mandatory item: whether the customer is a business or a private person, because that can affect the invoice fields and sometimes the tax treatment.
We can reflect all of this in A1 and then design A2 around it.

I agree with the proposal to start at confirmation and end at posting.
For mandatory data from movers, I would summarise it as:
- Customer details (name, address, business or private)
- Job date and location
- Service type (from a short list)
- Total billable hours or fixed price flag
- Extra billable items (tick boxes plus short note if needed)
- Job completion confirmation (for example, a simple yes or customer signature)
This feels manageable and should cover what we need for T1 and later for the job sheet in A2.

I am fine with not including the payment matching step in this process.
For the movers data, I just want to check if we also need distance or route information for any tax reasons, or if that is only for pricing.
If it is only for pricing, maybe we can keep it optional and let operations decide how they want to track it.
Once we confirm the list, I can help check a few recent jobs to see if we already have most of this information or if we need to change how we collect it.

On distance and route: from a tax and bookkeeping point of view, we do not need exact kilometres for each job as long as the price and VAT are correct and we can explain the service.
Distance is more relevant for pricing and planning, so I suggest we keep it optional for accounting and let operations decide if they want it for their own analysis.
Given the feedback so far, I propose we close two points:
1) Process scope: start at job confirmation with minimum customer and job details; end at invoice posting in the ledger.
2) Mandatory data from movers for accounting: customer details (including business or private), job date and address, service type from a list, total billable hours or fixed price flag, extra billable items, and job completion confirmation.
If anyone disagrees, please comment today; otherwise I will update A1 and T1 accordingly and treat this as agreed.

Works for me.
If the job sheet later keeps these items short and clear, I can fill them in without slowing down the team.
I will start paying more attention to marking business versus private customers in my notes so we can test this in the pilot.

No objections from me.
I will help by reviewing the first version of A1 once you update it, to make sure the steps and mandatory fields are clearly shown for both movers and bookkeepers.

Agreed as well.
Once A1 is updated, we can use it as the base for the training material later and for the quick-reference guides in A7.
I will also note these mandatory fields so we can check them when we design the job sheet in A2.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalise the standard moving job sheet for movers

messages.text:
I have put together a first draft of the moving job sheet for T2, based on what we agreed in TH1.
The draft is in A2 and includes:
- Customer details (name, address, business or private tick box)
- Job date and address
- Service type (local move, long-distance, packing, storage)
- Total hours (start, finish, breaks)
- Extra billable items (packing materials, extra stops, special handling)
- Job completion confirmation (customer signature or name)
From the truck side, it looks ok, but I am not sure if the layout works well for accounting.
Can the bookkeepers please review and tell me if anything is missing or too much?

Thanks for the draft, I have opened A2.
From an accounting point of view, the structure is close to what we need for T2 and later for posting rules in A3.
A few suggestions:
- Move the customer details and business/private tick box to the very top so they are always filled first.
- Add a small field for customer tax number for business customers.
- For service type, add a short code next to each option so we can map it directly to the correct revenue account and VAT code.
- For extra billable items, include a simple quantity and unit price column so we can reconcile with the invoice.
If we adjust these, I think the sheet will work well for both movers and bookkeepers.

I like the draft.
One concern: the current layout has the time fields spread across the page, which might lead to missing entries when things get busy.
Could we group start time, finish time, and breaks in one small table, and then have a single field for total billable hours that the mover can calculate or that we calculate in the office?
Also, for job completion, maybe we can allow either a signature or just the printed name of the customer plus a tick box that the job is complete, to keep it flexible.

From my side, I would add a small section for notes on damage or special situations.
Right now, movers sometimes send separate photos or messages, and it is hard to link them to the right job.
If we have a notes box on A2, we can refer to it when issuing the invoice or handling complaints.
Apart from that, I agree with the suggestions from the others.

I have a small question: do we need a field for distance on the job sheet, or is that handled elsewhere?
If we do not need it for accounting, maybe we can leave it out to keep the sheet shorter.
Also, I am not sure where to put the tools checklist from T5. Should it be on the same sheet or a separate one?

On distance, we do not need it for accounting, so I would keep it off the main job sheet to avoid clutter.
For the tools checklist in T5 and A5, I suggest we keep it as a separate checklist that can be stapled or attached to the job sheet.
That way, movers can run through the tools before and after each job without mixing it with customer and billing data.
If everyone agrees, we can finalise A2 without distance and with a reference to A5 for tools.

I can move the customer details to the top and add the tax number field.
For service type codes, could you share the codes you want to use so I do not invent something that does not match A3?
On the time table, grouping start, finish, and breaks sounds fine. I can still write the total hours if we add a small box for it.
I will update A2 with these changes and share a new version.

For the service type codes, we can start simple:
- LM for local move
- LD for long-distance
- PK for packing
- ST for storage
Later, when we finalise A3, we can map each code to the correct revenue account and VAT code.
If you add these codes next to the check boxes on A2, it will help us post consistently.

For the notes section, maybe we can add a small reminder text like: use this for damage, waiting time, or anything unusual.
That might help movers remember to write down things that could affect the invoice or later discussions.
Once the new version of A2 is ready, I can test it on two sample jobs to see if all fields are clear.

I have updated A2 with:
- Customer details and business/private tick box at the top, plus tax number field.
- Grouped time table with start, finish, breaks, and total hours box.
- Service type check boxes with LM, LD, PK, ST codes.
- Extra items table with quantity and unit price.
- Notes box with a short reminder text.
From my side, it still looks usable on the truck.
Can you check if this is now good enough to lock the fields and layout?

I have reviewed the updated A2 and it covers all mandatory data we agreed in TH1, plus what we need for T2 and later posting.
From an accounting and compliance angle, I am comfortable using this layout for the pilot.
Unless there are strong objections, I suggest we treat the current fields and layout as final for the pilot phase.
We can still refine after T8 and T10 based on feedback, but for now we need a stable version.
On submission, we also need to decide how movers will send the completed sheets: photos, scans, or paper drop-off.
My proposal is: movers take a clear photo at the end of the job and send it to a shared channel or email, and then drop off the paper at the depot at the end of the day for archiving.
Please react or comment so we can close both the layout and the submission method.

I support locking the current A2 for the pilot.
On submission, photos sent right after the job will help us issue invoices faster, while the paper copy will help with audit and filing.
We just need to make sure the photos are readable, so maybe we can add a short tip in the training and in A7 later.

Agreed on both points.
The layout is clear enough, and the photo plus paper drop-off approach should work.
We can test in T2 by using the sheet on two real moves and checking if the photos are good enough for invoicing.

From the truck side, I am ok with the current A2.
Taking a photo at the end of the job and sending it in is fine, as long as we have a clear place to send it.
I will try this on the next two moves and see how it goes.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on posting rules, tax treatment, and invoice templates

messages.text:
I have drafted the chart of accounts and posting rules for moving services in A3, and the invoice and quote templates in A4, covering T3, T4, and part of T6.
Key points in A3:
- Separate revenue accounts for local moves, long-distance, packing, and storage, aligned with the LM, LD, PK, ST codes from A2.
- Standard VAT code for domestic moves, with a note that cross-border or special cases must be checked with the tax advisor.
- Posting rules for typical transactions: standard move, move with packing materials, and move with storage.
In A4, the invoice and quote templates include all mandatory legal fields, customer tax number for business customers, and a clear breakdown of services and VAT.
Please review and comment on:
1) Whether the account structure is clear enough for daily posting.
2) Any missing scenarios in the posting rules.
3) Whether the invoice and quote templates are practical for our use and compliant with our obligations.

I have gone through A3 and A4.
On the chart of accounts, the separate revenue accounts per service type make sense and will help with reporting.
For posting rules, I would add an example for a job that includes both moving and storage, where storage is billed monthly.
On the invoice template in A4, I see all the usual legal fields, but I am not sure if we need a specific reference to the job sheet number from A2.
If we add a field for job sheet number, it will be easier to link invoices to the underlying documentation.

I like the structure in A3.
One question: for packing materials, do we treat them as part of the moving service revenue or as separate goods revenue?
From what I have seen, we usually include them in the service, but I want to be sure this is correct for tax and reporting.
On A4, the quote template mirrors the invoice nicely, which should reduce differences between what we promise and what we bill.

I have a small doubt about the VAT codes in A3.
For domestic moves, we use the standard VAT rate, but what about moves that start here and end in another country?
I do not feel confident deciding that, so I think we should have a clear note that these cases must be checked with the tax advisor before invoicing.
Maybe we can add a short section in A3 and T6 about special cases and who to contact.

Good points.
On job sheet numbers, I agree we should add a field on A4 to reference the job sheet from A2. That will help with audit trails and error tracking in A6.
On packing materials, my proposal is:
- Treat standard packing materials used as part of the move as service revenue under the same account and VAT code as the move.
- Only use a separate goods revenue account if we sell materials separately without a move.
This keeps things simple and aligned with how we actually work.
For cross-border moves, I agree with the concern. I will add a clear note in A3 and T6 that any cross-border or unusual tax situations must be checked with the tax advisor before issuing the invoice.
Please confirm if you are comfortable with this approach so we can move towards approving the chart of accounts and templates for the pilot.

I am fine with treating standard packing materials as part of the service revenue, and using a separate account only when we sell materials alone.
Adding the job sheet reference on A4 and the special case note in A3 and T6 should cover the main risks.
I would also suggest we include one worked example per service type in A3, showing the debit and credit entries, so that anyone posting can follow the pattern easily.

Agreed on the treatment of packing materials.
The worked examples idea is good; it will help reduce errors, especially when we are busy.
Once you add the job sheet field and the special case note, I think we can approve the chart of accounts and posting rules for the pilot.

Thanks for clarifying the cross-border point.
Adding a clear instruction to contact the tax advisor for those cases in A3 and T6 will help me know when to stop and ask.
I will not try to decide those cases myself.
With that in place, I am ok with the posting rules and templates for the pilot.

I have updated A3 and A4 with:
- Job sheet reference field on the invoice and quote templates.
- Clear note that cross-border and unusual tax cases must be checked with the tax advisor before invoicing.
- Worked examples for each main service type, including combined move and storage.
From my side, A3 and A4 are now ready for pilot use.
Unless there are further comments today, I propose we formally approve the chart of accounts and posting rules, and also approve the invoice and quote templates for the pilot.
This will allow us to complete T3, T4, and move forward with T6.

No further comments from me.
I consider the chart of accounts and posting rules in A3, and the templates in A4, approved for the pilot.
We can still refine them after we see real data in T8 and log issues in A6.

Agreed.
The structure is clear, and the examples will help a lot.
I will start using the new posting rules from A3 for any pilot jobs and note any issues in A6 as part of T9.

I am also ok with approving A3 and A4 for the pilot.
I will follow the worked examples closely and use the error log in A6 if I make any mistakes so we can correct them properly.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and coordinate the pilot and training sessions

messages.text:
With A2, A3, and A4 ready for pilot, we need to plan the pilot scope and training, covering T7, T8, and T12.
Proposal for pilot scope:
- Include 5 to 7 moves over the next two weeks.
- Mix of local and long-distance jobs, with at least one including packing.
- Use the new job sheet A2, tools checklist A5, posting rules A3, and templates A4 for these jobs.
For training, I suggest one joint session of 60 minutes with movers and bookkeepers together, plus a short written quick-reference from A7.
We also need to agree a pilot start date and who must attend the training before we start.
Please share which upcoming moves would be good candidates and your availability for a training session.

Looking at the schedule, I see:
- Two local moves early next week.
- One long-distance move mid-week.
- Another local move with packing at the end of the week.
These four could be part of the pilot.
If we need more, we can add one or two from the following week.
For training, mornings before 9 are usually best for me, or late afternoon after we return.

From the accounting side, I would like the pilot to start at the beginning of a week so we can track the full flow from job to posting.
If we aim for next Monday as the pilot start date, we can schedule training later this week.
For training content in T7, we can walk through:
- The new process map in A1.
- How to fill in A2 and A5.
- How invoices and postings will look using A3 and A4.
I am available most afternoons this week.

I support starting the pilot on a Monday.
For the moves, the four that were mentioned sound like a good mix. We can add one more local move from the second week to reach at least five for T8.
On training, I think we should invite:
- All movers who might work on the pilot jobs.
- The bookkeepers who will issue invoices and post entries.
- The operations supervisor, if possible, so they understand the new steps.
A 60-minute joint session should be enough if we keep it focused and use A7 as a handout.

I am ok with next Monday as a pilot start date.
For training, I would prefer late afternoon, as mornings are often busy with calls and emails.
I can help prepare the attendance list and capture key questions during the session for follow-up in A8.

Based on the input, here is a concrete proposal:
- Pilot start date: next Monday.
- Pilot scope: 5 moves over two weeks (the four identified by 395422 plus one additional local move in week two).
- Training session: this Thursday at 16:00, 60 minutes, with movers, bookkeepers, and the operations supervisor invited.
During the training we will use A1, A2, A5, A3, A4, and share the quick-reference from A7.
If there are no major conflicts, I will confirm this plan with operations and accounting management as part of T12.

Thursday at 16:00 works for me.
The four moves I mentioned are still on the schedule, and adding one more local move in week two should be fine.
I will let the other movers know about the training time once it is confirmed.

I can join Thursday at 16:00 and support with the part on invoices and postings.
Next Monday as pilot start is also fine.
I suggest we document the agreed pilot moves and dates in A8 so we can track which jobs are in scope.

All good from my side.
I will help during the training by walking through a sample job from A2 to A4 so everyone sees the full flow.
We can also explain the daily async check-in ritual for the pilot and how we will use A8 to capture feedback.

Thursday 16:00 works for me too.
I will prepare the attendance list and a simple template to capture questions and issues during the session, which we can then add into A8.
Looking forward to seeing how the full process works in practice next week.

threads.thread_goal: Monitor pilot progress, log issues, and refine the process

messages.text:
Pilot check-in: the first two pilot moves using A2, A5, A3, and A4 are now completed.
Quick numbers:
- 2 moves processed with the new job sheet A2 and tools checklist A5.
- 2 invoices issued and posted using the new rules in A3 and templates in A4.
We have also started logging issues in A6 and feedback in A8 as part of T8, T9, and T10.
Please share any problems you saw on the truck or in the office so we can refine the process and templates.

From the truck side on the first two jobs:
- Filling in A2 was ok, but I almost forgot the business/private tick box once.
- The time table worked well, but I had to think twice about where to write breaks.
- A5 for tools was quick to run through before and after the job.
One issue: taking a clear photo of A2 in low light at the end of the day was a bit tricky. I had to retake it to make sure it was readable.
I have added this as feedback in A8.

On the accounting side:
- The job sheet photos were mostly readable, but one was slightly blurred, which made the tax number hard to read.
- Posting using A3 was straightforward; the service codes from A2 matched the accounts well.
- I logged one error in A6 where I initially used the wrong VAT code and then corrected it.
For improvements, I suggest we add a small reminder on A2 near the business/private tick box, as it seems easy to miss when in a hurry.

I have added a few entries to A6 for minor issues:
- Missing customer tax number on one job sheet.
- Unclear handwriting on extra items.
- One case where the job sheet number was not copied to the invoice.
All were corrected, but they show where we can improve.
For T10, I think we should consider:
- Making the business/private tick box more visible on A2.
- Adding a short example of how to write extra items clearly.
- Emphasising the job sheet number field in A4 during training refresh.

I have been helping maintain A8 with feedback from the training and the first pilot jobs.
Some comments from movers:
- They like having standard service codes, but a small legend on the back of A2 would help new staff.
- They asked if we can pre-print some customer details for regular clients to save time.
From bookkeepers:
- They appreciate the job sheet reference on A4.
- They would like a simple checklist for what to verify before posting, which we could add to A7 or as a small box on A2.

Thanks for the detailed feedback.
For immediate refinements under T10 and T11, I propose we make three concrete changes:
1) On A2, highlight the business/private tick box and add a short reminder text.
2) On the back of A2, add a small legend for the service codes and an example of how to write extra items.
3) In A7, add a short pre-posting checklist for bookkeepers: check customer details, tax number, job sheet number, and VAT code.
These changes should not disrupt the pilot but will address the main issues we have seen so far.
I will draft updated versions and share them for a quick review.

Those changes sound good to me.
Highlighting the business/private tick box will help, and a legend on the back of A2 will be useful for new movers.
For the photo issue, maybe we can also add a short tip in A7 about taking photos in good light and checking readability before sending.

I agree with the three proposed changes.
The pre-posting checklist in A7 will help reduce errors, especially when we are handling several invoices at once.
Once you share the updated A2 and A7, I can quickly check them against A3 and T6 to ensure they still align with the posting rules and compliance guideline.

No objections from me.
I will continue to log any new issues in A6 and A8 as the remaining pilot moves are completed.
At the end of T8, we can summarise the top issues and confirm if any further template changes are needed.

I can help by checking that the updated A2 and A7 are consistent with the training material from T7.
If needed, we can send a short update message to movers and bookkeepers explaining the small changes so they are not surprised.

Update: I have uploaded revised versions of A2 and A7 with the agreed tweaks.
For the rest of the pilot, let us continue to:
- Use the updated A2 and A5 on all pilot moves.
- Log any errors and corrections in A6 under T9.
- Capture feedback and improvement ideas in A8 for T10.
At the end of the pilot, we will run a short retrospective and then freeze the final versions for wider rollout.
